record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a truncated file listing only; code and linked documents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes using mechanistic discovery and refusal interventions to study how candidate rankings transfer between intervention operators. It does not test the specific harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction in the claim.
record.gate_note: The README reports aggregate operator-reliability and proxy-validation results, but no outcome for ablating or adding the claimed single direction. The listed experiment and result files are not evidence that their contents were read or run. The README also says matched discovery methods beat controls, without giving a numerical result for that comparison.
record.test_reason: The repository studies attention-head candidate sets for selective refusal under different operators (head ablation, mean/probe steering, patching) and reports ranking agreement and selection regret. It does not compute or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless residual direction and reports no refusal rate from removing or adding such a direction. Its results bear on intervention-method reliability, not on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that matched discovery methods still beat controls, so circuit discovery does not fail; rather, intervention reliability needs direct validation under the intended operator.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes candidate discovery and interventions involving ablation, activation replacement, edge/path patching, and steering; it does not state that the original harmful-minus-harmless residual direction method is used. Repository type: research tool/study repository.
record.method_sensitivity: Candidate-ranking agreement differs between repeated and cross-operator comparisons; the generation-proxy summary excludes one generation-collapse cell.

fits_no_version.finding: For selective-refusal head-set candidates, same-operator split-half Spearman is 0.881 versus 0.077 across operators. Plausible-only crossed transfers have positive regret in 51/72 cases and the same winner in 12/72.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-relevant component rankings are reliable under a repeated intervention operator but transfer poorly across operators.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 168 directional transfers, lower cross-operator agreement predicts greater normalized regret on untouched data (rho = -0.553, CI [-0.629, -0.408]).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-operator agreement predicts selection regret for intervention candidates.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal logit proxy has median baseline AUC 0.711. Its intervention effects correlate with generated-refusal effects at rho = 0.687 (one generation-collapse cell excluded), with matching signs in 14/23 cells.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal logit proxies are informative about, but not interchangeable with, generated-refusal measures of intervention effects.

record.problems: The README gives aggregate summaries rather than per-model results or prompt-level evidence. It does not provide direct results for the claimed single-direction intervention or a general-capability assessment. The code and linked result documents were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results extracted from the file listing; listed result files were not inspected. The README's statement that matched discovery methods beat controls has no numerical result in the provided text.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means direction ablation and addition, effect on refusal rates, and capability retention. Head-set interventions are not the claimed direction.
Jailbreak mechanism and adversarial training against ablation.
Multi-dimensional, affine or cone structure of refusal.
Separation of harmfulness encoding from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages or model variants. The WildGuard-to-HarmBench transfer is dataset transfer of head candidates, not direction transfer.
Role of training in whether one removable direction exists.
Reasoning models. A gpt-oss follow-on script is listed but no results appear in the README.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly unlinked (versions none). The README's aggregate figures cover both behaviours; the rows correctly take the selective-refusal column, except r5, which pools 168 transfers across both behaviours. The file listing shows five refusal models (llama32_1b/3b, qwen25_0.5b/1.5b/7b) plus a Gemma 2 9B follow-on. The interventions target attention-head sets, not a residual direction.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-minus-harmless residual direction, all-layer/all-position ablation, added-direction refusal, and collateral general capability.
Weight-edit removal of the claimed direction in released models.
Jailbreak suppression of the claimed direction and training robustness against its ablation.
Whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Effects of how or when refusal is trained on the existence of a removable direction.
